title: Investigating Light/Dark Locomotion in Larval Zebrafish Using a Behavioral Assay
author: Hillman, Kearn, et al.

steps.title: Run baseline locomotion recording
steps.instruction: Start a baseline recording in the Zantiks MWP using the ZANSCRIPT tracking script (OSF). The script runs three cycles of 5 min light followed by 5 min dark, for a total of 30 min. If recording more than one 96‑well plate, insert a 5‑min pause between successive baseline recordings to allow time for drug exposures.

steps.title: Prepare 10X drug solutions
steps.instruction: Immediately after starting the baseline recording, prepare 10X drug solutions in a 96‑well plate as described in Table 1, keeping rows C and F empty. Include a vehicle control well containing a 10X DMSO solution that will yield a final concentration of 0.5 % DMSO (i.e., 5.0 % DMSO in the 10X plate). Ensure each well contains a final volume of 500 µL.

substeps.instruction: For a 0 µM (vehicle) well: add 25 µL DMSO and 475 µL embryo medium.
For a 0.55 µM exposure: add 0.125 µL of 0.1 mM stock solution and 475 µL embryo medium.
For a 5 µM exposure: add 12.5 µL of 10 mM stock, 22.5 µL DMSO, and 475 µL embryo medium.
For a 50 µM exposure: add 25 µL of 10 mM stock and 475 µL embryo medium.
For a 500 µM exposure: add 5 µL of 1 M stock, 22.5 µL DMSO, and 475 µL embryo medium.
For a 5 000 µM exposure: add 25 µL of 1 M stock and 475 µL embryo medium.

steps.title: Add 10X solutions to larvae
steps.instruction: Add 25 µL of each prepared 10X solution to the corresponding well containing 4 dpf zebrafish larvae (16 larvae per plate). This yields a final exposure volume of at least 30 µL per well, minimizing pipetting error, and results in a final DMSO concentration of 0.5 % (v/v) for all wells.

steps.title: Normalize movement data in R
steps.instruction: Import the raw tracking data into the provided custom R script. Normalize movement by calculating the percentage of movement per minute per fish relative to the overall baseline locomotion. Remove tracking outliers using the median absolute deviation (MAD) method.

steps.title: Perform power and sample‑size analysis
steps.instruction: Run the R script’s power analysis module on the normalized data. Use a preliminary experiment size of n = 16 larvae per concentration. If the observed statistical power is greater than 0.8 and the required sample size is less than 16, retain n = 16 for the final experiment.

steps.title: Statistical testing of behavioral data
steps.instruction: Test the normality and distribution of the normalized movement data. Then apply the chosen statistical analyses (e.g., linear mixed‑effects models with fish as a random effect) to assess treatment effects.
